Topic: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations (PDEs)

Target audience: University STEM students

Section: section_1 — The Concept: From ODEs to PDEs

Lecture lines:
ODEs track change in one variable, like time.
PDEs track change across both space and time.
Think of a point moving on a line.
Contrast this with ripples across a pond's surface.
PDEs capture this complex spatial evolution.

Planned animations:
Create title text "From ODEs to PDEs" in #FFFFFF.
Show ODE x(t) changing with respect to time.
Transition to PDE u(x,t) adding spatial dependency.
Highlight variable change: t becomes x and t.
Finalize view showing transition structure clearly.

Section: section_2 — Core Mechanism: The Partial Derivative

Lecture lines:
Partial derivatives act as a slice of reality.
Vary space while freezing time to see change.
Vary time while freezing space for local change.

Planned animations:
Title "The Partial Derivative" in #FFFFFF appears.
Draw 3D surface representing u(x,y).
Show tangent line along x-axis moving.
Highlight slope change as partial derivative u_x.
Return to surface with u_y visualization.

Section: section_3 — The Heat Equation: Modeling Diffusion

Lecture lines:
The heat equation models how energy spreads.
Visualize heat diffusing through a metal bar.
The center cools as heat moves outward.

Planned animations:
Title "The Heat Equation" in #FFFFFF appears.
Draw distribution graph u(x,t) at t=0.
Animate diffusion spreading the peak over time.
Show heat flux vectors pointing outward.
Fade graph to indicate steady state.

Section: section_4 — The Wave Equation: Modeling Oscillation

Lecture lines:
The wave equation tracks acceleration and movement.
A guitar string shows space-time interaction.
It models the snap-back force of vibrations.

Planned animations:
Title "The Wave Equation" in #FFFFFF appears.
Create sine wave shape for u(x,t).
Animate oscillation back and forth.
Highlight velocity constant c in equation.
Freeze wave to show spatial pattern.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Real-World Impact

Lecture lines:
PDEs are the mathematical language of nature.
They govern everything from weather to finance.
We move from tracking points to fields.

Planned animations:
Title "Summary & Impact" in #FFFFFF.
Display equation summary collage of PDEs.
Show icons representing weather, finance, engineering.
Highlight connection to real-world modeling.
Fade out with final key concept summary.

Maintain stylistic cohesion by avoiding the mixture of disparate asset types; specifically, do not use pixel-art or figurative representational icons alongside minimalist abstract vector mobjects.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("The Wave Equation: Modeling Oscillation", [
            "The wave equation tracks acceleration and movement.",
            "A guitar string shows space-time interaction.",
            "It models the snap-back force of vibrations."
        ])

        # Animation Setup
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(wave, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        eq = MathTex(r"\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'A4')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), Create(wave))
        self.play(Write(eq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE), FadeIn(eq.copy().set_color(BLUE)))
        # Oscillating wave
        v_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        wave.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * x + v_tracker.get_value()), x_range=[-1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        ))
        self.play(v_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * np.pi), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        wave.remove_updater(wave.get_updaters()[0])
        self.play(eq[0][-4:].animate.set_color(GREEN)) # Highlight c^2 part
        self.wait(1)
